[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [agency] "So Eliphaz says this in accusing Job" vs "Ταῦτα οὖν λέγει, ἐγκαλῶν τῷ Ἰὼβ": Subject is 'he' (the commentator/author), not Eliphaz; commentator paraphrases, not Eliphaz speaking directly.; [completeness] "that he took away the clothing of the naked" vs "ὅτι ἀμφίασιν γυμνῶν ἀφεῖλεν": Missing 'clothing' translation issue: ἀμφίασιν is 'clothing' but context suggests this is commentator's gloss, not accusation; however more critically, the Greek has no 'he' specified as Job here in the same way—the commentator states this as what 'he says' in accusing.; [modality] "is liable to judgment" vs "ὑπεύθυνον": Added 'to judgment' not in Greek; ὑπεύθυνον means 'liable/answerable' absolutely, no 'judgment' specified.; [agency] "He points out that we ought to extend our good deeds" vs "ἐπισημαίνει δὲ μέχρι τοσούτου εὐεργεσίας ἐκτείνειν ὀφείλομεν": Subject of ἐπισημαίνει is the commentator/author ('he marks/signifies'), not a new 'He'; 'we ought' (ὀφείλομεν) is correct but 'He points out' obscures that this is the commentator's exegesis continuing.; [negation] "Just as we receive a reward for a cup of cold water, so he condemns Job for great harshness" vs "Ὥσπερ οὖν διὰ τὸ ποτήριον ψυχροῦ ὕδατος μισθὸν λαμβάνομεν, πολλὴν μέντοι ἀπηνίαν τοῦ Ἰὼβ καταψηφίζεται": Corrupted comparison: 'Just as...so' makes parallel, but Greek has 'Therefore just as through cup of cold water reward we receive, much indeed harshness of Job he condemns'—the μέντοι is adversative ('however/yet'), making contrast not parallel: 'just as we receive reward... yet/instead he condemns Job for much harshness'.; [agency] "as one who did not even provide water" vs "ὡς μηδὲ ὕδωρ τὴν ἀδάπανον χάριν παρέχοντος": παρέχοντος is genitive absolute/participial construction with Job as object of condemnation, but 'as one who' adds a noun not in Greek; more seriously, the syntax is 'as [him] not even providing water'—the translation's 'one who' is interpretive but acceptable. However, 'the gift that costs nothing' for τὴν ἀδάπανον χάριν is fine.; [modality] "What do I mean, he says, by saying you did not provide for the one in need?" vs "Τί λέγω, φησὶν, ὅτι οὐ παρέσχες τῷ δεομένῳ;": Wrong speech act: 'What do I mean by saying' for Τί λέγω is wrong; this is 'What do I say?' or 'What am I to say?'—a rhetorical question of exasperation, not self-explanation of meaning. 'By saying' is added, changing the syntax.; [completeness] "Since you even took away the small comfort of bread from the hungry man" vs "ὅποτε καὶ τὴν μικρὰν παραμυθίαν τοῦ ἄρτου παρὰ τοῦ πεινῶντος ἀφείλου": Missing 'from beside/from the presence of' (παρὰ τοῦ); 'from the hungry man' loses the παρά = 'from beside/away from' which emphasizes taking right from him. Also 'comfort of bread' for παραμυθίαν τοῦ ἄρτου is acceptable but 'consolation of bread' closer. | part 2/5: [completeness] "For God commanded us to fight on behalf of helpless souls. More than other people, the poor, widows, and orphans need help." vs "Οὐδένα μὲν γὰρ δεῖ κακοῦν, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ χρὴ φείδεσθαι τῶν ὀρφανῶν·": Two invented clauses not in Greek source text.; [negation] "not justly or without passion" vs "οὐ δικαίως, οὐδὲ ἀπαθῶς": Greek has double negation 'not justly, nor without passion'; English 'or' obscures both are negated. | part 3/5: [agency] "For God commanded us to fight" vs "περὶ γὰρ τῶν ἀβοηθήτων ψυχῶν πολεμεῖν ὁ Θεὸς ἐνετείλατο": Subject is 'God commanded,' not 'God commanded us'; no 'us' in source; [completeness] ""But the counsel of the impious is far from him"" vs "Βουλὴ δὲ ἀσεβῶν πόῤῥω ἀπ' αὐτοῦ": Missing verse number ιηʹ (18); 'him' ambiguous but acceptable; [completeness] ""Bring forth confession from his mouth"" vs "Ἔκβαλε δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐξηγορίαν": Missing verse number κβʹ (22); 'his' for αὐτοῦ but context suggests God's mouth; [modality] "Acknowledge your sins" vs "Ἐξομολόγησαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων σου": Imperative 'confess' softened to 'acknowledge'; same root but command weakened; [modality] "be instructed by God" vs "ὑπαγορεύθητι παρὰ Θεοῦ": Passive imperative 'be dictated to' softened to 'be instructed'; [scripture] ""Behold, I have put my words in your mouth" (Jeremiah 1:9)" vs "ὡς ὕστερον Ἱερεμίας ἤκουσεν": Source only says 'as later Jeremiah heard'; quotation and reference are supplied by translator | part 4/5: [agency] "If you are righteous and worthy, be instructed by God" vs "Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου": Source is God's speech to Jeremiah, not conditional exhortation to be instructed; [source_identity] "as Jeremiah later heard" vs "Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου": Source quotes Jeremiah 1:9 directly, not 'later heard'; [modality] "If you are righteous and worthy" vs "Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου": Added conditional 'if' not in source; source is declarative quotation; [completeness] "Yet beyond my strength, or outside my action, the reproof has been laid upon me" vs "Οἶδα, φησὶν, ὅτι ἐκ τῶν πράξεων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῖς": Final clause 'the judgments to them' dropped; 'Yet beyond my strength' is invented; [agency] "you think you bring reproofs against me" vs "δοκεῖτε τοὺς ἐλέγχους ἐπάγειν": Subject is 'you' plural addressing Job's friends, not 'you think you bring' | part 5/5: [source_identity] ""I know," he says, "that from the actions of men come their judgments" vs "πλὴν ὑπὲρ τὴν ἰσχύν μου": Invented clause not in source; no 'actions of men' or 'judgments' in Greek; [modality] "he will not use threat against me" vs "εἶτα ἐν ἀπειλῇ μοι οὐ χρήσεται": Missing 'then' (εἶτα); future statement rendered as negated future rather than 'then he will not use'; [modality] "may he bring my judgment to an end" vs "ἐξαγάγοι δὲ εἰς τέλος τὸ κρίμα μου": Optative 'may he bring out' weakened to simple wish; 'bring out' lost; [agency] "not as though God were now about to judge him" vs "οὐχ ὡς νῦν μέλλοντος αὐτοῦ κρίνειν": Subject is 'he' (God/Job's interlocutor), not 'God' specifically; 'him' wrong person; [completeness] "Among the Hebrews, "end" and "victory" are signified by one word" vs "Παρ' Ἑβραίοις, τὸ τέλος καὶ ἡ νίκη διὰ μιᾶς σημαίνεται λέξεως": Missing 'by one word' should be 'through one word'; διὰ μιᾶς λέξεως = 'through one word'
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [source_identity] "So Eliphaz says this in accusing Job, that he took away the clothing of the naked." vs "Ταῦτα οὖν λέγει, ἐγκαλῶν τῷ Ἰὼβ, ὅτι ἀμφίασιν γυμνῶν ἀφεῖλεν.": Eliphaz is not in the Greek; speaker identity is invented. | part 5/5: [source_identity] ""I know," he says, "that from the actions of men come their judgments." vs "πλὴν ὑπὲρ τὴν ἰσχύν μου ἐπετέθη μοι, ἤτοι ἔξω τῆς πράξεώς μου, ὁ ἔλεγχος.": Invented clause not in source; Greek says 'Yet beyond my strength was laid upon me...the reproof,' not 'from the actions of men come their judgments.'; [completeness] "not as though God were now about to judge him." vs "οὐχ ὡς νῦν μέλλοντος αὐτοῦ κρίνειν": Dropped pronoun 'me'; source says 'not as now being about to judge me,' not 'judge him.'

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'Eliphaz' names the speaker of Job 22, the implied subject of Ταῦτα οὖν λέγει, ἐγκαλῶν τῷ Ἰώβ. 'For God commanded us to fight on behalf of helpless souls. More than other people, the poor, widows, and orphans need help' renders περὶ γὰρ τῶν ἀβοηθήτων ψυχῶν πολεμεῖν ὁ Θεὸς ἐνετείλατο. Πλέον δὲ παρὰ τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους, πτωχοί, χῆραι, ὀρφανοὶ δέονται βοηθείας, which is in the Greek. So is 'I know, he says, that from the actions of men come their judgments' (Οἶδα, φησίν, ὅτι ἐκ τῶν πράξεων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῖς); the 'invented' flags came from chunk boundaries. Jeremiah 1:9 (Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὸ στόμα σου) is quoted in the Greek. 'Just as … so' gives the force of Ὥσπερ … μέντοι. Τί λέγω, φησίν, ὅτι οὐ παρέσχες …; ὅποτε καί … ἀφείλου is the rhetorical 'What do I mean by saying you did not provide …? You even took away …'. 'Acknowledge', 'be instructed' and 'liable to judgment' are idiom.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. Eliphaz is the speaker of Job 22, the implied subject of λέγει. The 'invented' clause is the commentator's Οἶδα, φησίν, ὅτι ἐκ τῶν πράξεων τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῖς, which is in the Greek. In οὐχ ὡς νῦν μέλλοντος αὐτοῦ κρίνειν, αὐτοῦ is God, the subject of the genitive absolute ('not as though he were now about to judge'). The supplied object 'him' is Job, who is speaking of himself in the third person in the paraphrase; the sense is unchanged.
